}}

{{recipe}}

This variation on a classic cheese-flavored risotto is hearty and delicious. The beer adds a Welsh Rarebit overtone. The best beer is malty, not hoppy. A good amber or Belgian ale works well.

==Ingredients==
*½ large [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] uncooked [[Cookbook:Rice|arborio rice]]
*1½ cups hot [[Cookbook:Stock|vegetable stock]] (approximate)
*½ cup [[Cookbook:Beer|beer]]
*¼ cup [[Cookbook:Grater|grated]] [[Cookbook:Parmesan Cheese|Parmesan cheese]]
*¼ cup shredded sharp [[Cookbook:Cheddar Cheese|cheddar cheese]] (to taste)

==Procedure==

# Heat the stock to near [[Cookbook:Boiling|boiling]]. Keep hot.
# [[Cookbook:Sweat|Sweat]] the onion in a heavy, medium [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]] with the olive oil, adding a generous pinch of [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]. When the onions are soft and transparent, add the rice, [[Cookbook:Sautéing|sautéeing]] until each grain is coated.
# Add the beer and heat to [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]], stirring constantly. When the beer is mostly absorbed, add around ⅓ to ½ cup of hot stock. Stir constantly while simmering. Repeat procedure for around twenty minutes—most of the stock should be consumed and the rice should be tender to the taste before proceeding. The rice will produce a thick, creamy sauce in the course of cooking (see [[Cookbook:Risotto|risotto]]).
# Remove from heat, adding the Parmesan cheese and stirring to incorporate. Give the cheese a chance to dissolve and melt, then add the cheddar. Stir to melt and incorporate. If a cheesier rice is desired, add more.
